content:
The image shows a very young soybean seedling emerging from wet, dark soil. The seedling is at the cotyledon/early emergence stage and appears stunted or collapsed at the soil line. The hypocotyl looks like it may have a soft, water-soaked rot near the soil surface. There are no developed leaves to assess foliar symptoms. The soil appears very wet/saturated.

Key observations:
- Seedling is barely emerged, appears weak and wilting/collapsed
- Soil is very wet and dark (waterlogged conditions)
- The seedling shows signs of damping-off (soft collapse near soil line)
- No reddish-brown firm cankers (rules out Rhizoctonia)
- The wet, saturated soil and soft seedling collapse are consistent with water-mold pathogens
- Pythium damping-off thrives in wet, cool conditions and causes water-soaked soft rot of hypocotyls/roots, pre- or post-emergence damping off
- Phytophthora could also cause this, but typically shows brown chocolate-colored stem lesion extending upward from soil — less visible here
- The soft, collapsed appearance at/below soil line in saturated conditions strongly points to Pythium
